question: Based on Fig. ccd8e7b4, During which months do hatchlings of the species shown in the image typically appear?

text_evidence:
The lizard in the image corresponds to Greater earless lizard. The greater earless lizard (Cophosaurus montanus) is the sole species in the "Cophosaurus" genus. These lizards lack external ear openings, aiding in burrowing, and have other sand-burrowing adaptations like a recessed lower jaw and flared upper labial scales. Sexually dimorphic, males are larger, with distinctive bold blue bars on their sides.

Native to the Sonoran Desert and arid regions of Southeastern USA and central Mexico, they inhabit areas with dense vegetation, rocks, gravel, and sand. They are oviparous, laying 3–12 eggs per clutch, with hatchlings appearing from May to September.

The greater earless lizard (Cophosaurus texanus) is the sole species in the "Cophosaurus" genus. Closely related to lesser earless lizards in the "Holbrookia" genus, it was once classified under "Holbrookia texana" from 1852 to the 1970s. These lizards lack external ear openings, aiding in burrowing, and have other sand-burrowing adaptations like a recessed lower jaw and flared upper labial scales. Sexually dimorphic, males are larger and more colorful, especially in the breeding season, with distinctive bold black bars on their sides.

Native to the Chihuahua Desert and arid regions of Southwestern USA and northern Mexico, they inhabit areas with sparse vegetation, rocks, gravel, and sand. Their coloration often matches the local environment for camouflage. Greater earless lizards are insectivores, feeding on crickets, grasshoppers, and other insects, and occasionally spiders and small lizards. They are oviparous, laying 2–9 eggs per clutch, with hatchlings appearing from June to October.
